instruction: A listening-station display has two citation slots and a budget of 100 printed characters across the two excerpts. Choose exactly two distinct slips about the station's recording. Their combined evidence must document all three stages: capture, copying, and mastering. Stage flags are 0 or 1 and describe what the slip directly documents. Print sizes are positive integer character counts supplied by layout, including citation labels. Among feasible pairs maximize the sum of the slips' curator detail scores, measured in integer points. Break ties by smaller total print size and then by the lexicographically smallest ordered pair of slip IDs. All fields are non-null and slip IDs are unique. Return the single winning row with columns first_slip, second_slip, detail_points, print_chars, placing the smaller slip ID first. Return zero rows if no pair fits. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Audit adjacent sightings in each object's documented itinerary. Integer visit_no gives the established visit order within the object, with gaps allowed. Each cited note places the object at a gallery on one unknown integer day between early_day and late_day inclusive, measured from the same catalogue epoch. For each adjacent pair in visit order, consult the minimum elapsed days for its directed route. Report a conflict only if even the most favorable choice of days for that pair falls short. Scope is pairwise feasibility only. Skip same-gallery pairs and routes without a recorded minimum. Return object_code, from_note, to_note, shortfall_days, ordered by object_code in binary order then by the destination visit_no ascending. shortfall_days is the positive difference between the required minimum and the maximum possible elapsed days. Note IDs, visit numbers within objects, and directed route keys are unique. All fields are non-null. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Calculate interest payable for each deposit account for days 1 through 4 inclusive. opening_cents is the balance immediately before day 1. Each movement is a separate signed posting in cents that takes effect before that day's close. Include all postings on an in-scope day, including multiple postings on the same day. Ignore postings outside the period. A day without postings carries forward the preceding balance. All closing balances are nonnegative. Interest accrues at 3 basis points per day on each closing balance, without compounding. Round the four-day interest total once to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded upward. Account codes are unique in deposit_openings, and no fields are null. Return account_code, balance_day_cents (the sum of the four closing balances), and interest_cents, ordered by account_code ascending. Include accounts without movements. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Produce frozen_locations.csv representing the archive catalog at the end of minute 30. Each catalog_event is a complete update for one segment. A non-NULL shelf_code places the segment on that shelf, replacing any earlier placement. A NULL shelf_code withdraws the segment until a subsequent placement. Apply only events with minute_no at or before 30, in increasing minute_no order, breaking same-minute ties by increasing event_no. event_no is globally unique and need not increase across different minutes. All fields except shelf_code are non-NULL. Segments start absent. Include only segments present at freeze, with columns segment_id, shelf_code, placement_event (the event_no of the controlling placement). Sort by shelf_code ascending, then segment_id ascending, using binary text order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.
